articleBlocks: Pinpoint #532 uses Chest, Dough, Hazel, Coco, and Pea to hide a simple suffix pattern. The clues look like food words at first, especially with Chest, Hazel, Coco, and Pea, but Dough makes the category less literal. The clean connection appears when each clue is attached to the same ending, turning scattered food hints into one word-building solve. That shift matters because the puzzle is testing compound formation more than ingredients or botanical categories.

Chest becomes chestnut, Hazel becomes hazelnut, Coco becomes coconut, and Pea becomes peanut. Dough is the clue that prevents the answer from being just types of nuts, because doughnut fits the spelling and phrase pattern even though it is a pastry.
The full board confirms the answer as words that come before nut. A literal food or tree answer cannot explain every clue as cleanly as the compound-word pattern does.
The answer is words that come before nut: chestnut, doughnut, hazelnut, coconut, and peanut.
